clue.text: Belief I can become helpful

indicators.note: the letters of the first three words become something else, rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A motivational slogan: if you believe in yourself, you can turn into someone useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become' tells you to rearrange BELIEFICAN, the letters of 'Belief I can'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beneficial does good or brings advantage, so it is useful and helpful.

clue.text: Looked injured, so left in bed

indicators.note: the letter for left is placed inside the word bed

explanation.surface: Someone feigning injury was told to stay lying down in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who bled was losing blood, so they showed a wound and appeared hurt.

clue.text: Boring type expelled from dinner-dance

indicators.note: the letters are pushed out of the middle of dinner-dance, a run sitting inside those words

explanation.surface: A dull guest was thrown out of a formal evening of dining and dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerd is a dull, obsessive person, the kind others call a bore.

clue.text: Swat up for such a documentary?

definitions.text: Swat up for such a documentary?

parts.words: Swat up for such a documentary?
parts.note: an insect on a wall is the thing you would swat, and a documentary that observes unseen is named after that insect's viewpoint

explanation.surface: A student is advised to study hard for a particular kind of film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swat up' sounds like revising (British 'swot up'), but here it means hit something that is up on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A documentary filmed unobtrusively, as if by an unnoticed observer on the wall, is given this name.

clue.text: Composer is about to accept a lift

parts.note: C, short for Latin circa, means about
to hop in is to get into a car when offered a ride

explanation.surface: A musician is on the point of taking a ride from someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederic Chopin was a Polish composer of piano music.

clue.text: A communist called in and ordered

indicators.note: the word for called sits inside the word for communist

parts.note: a red is a communist, from the colour of the flag

explanation.surface: A Communist Party member was summoned and given instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Things arranged are put in order, set out neatly or sorted.

clue.text: Margin of advantage

explanation.surface: A short phrase describing a narrow lead in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is a border or rim; it is also a slight superiority over a rival.

clue.text: Realm visited at night — it's fantastic

definitions.text: Realm visited at night — it's fantastic

parts.words: Realm visited at night — it's fantastic
parts.note: the place you go while asleep is an imaginary one, fantastic in the sense of belonging to fantasy

explanation.surface: Praise for a wonderful kingdom that tourists explore after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' reads as praise, but it means unreal, born of fantasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream world is an imagined place of illusion, the land you inhabit while sleeping.

clue.text: Undergo a remarkable happening

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to live through an extraordinary event.
explanation.definitionFit: To experience something is to go through it; an experience is also a memorable event.

clue.text: Two or three actually late

parts.note: two or three in the morning are called early though they are really very late at night

explanation.surface: A complaint that a couple of people turned up behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two or three' looks like a few people; it is the time, 2 or 3 a.m.
explanation.definitionFit: The small hours after midnight, such as 2 or 3 a.m., go by this name.

clue.text: Either way, a shrill little call

indicators.note: the word reads the same forwards or backwards, whichever way you take it

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Whatever happens, a bird gives a thin high cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A peep is a faint, high chirp like that of a young bird.

clue.text: Capitally-rounded projectile aimed

parts.note: a bullet is a projectile fired from a gun
headed means directed or aimed at

explanation.surface: A missile was pointed at something, with a rounded tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capitally' means as to the head (Latin caput), so the definition describes a round head.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bullet-headed has a small round skull; the word also means obstinate.

clue.text: Nice weather, lately

parts.note: pleasant warm days arriving late in the year, after summer should have ended

explanation.surface: A remark that the weather has been pleasant recently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lately' reads as recently, but it means late in the season, in autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell of warm, sunny weather in autumn is given this name.

clue.text: He's in suspense, as he's powerless to proceed

definitions.text: He's in suspense, as he's powerless to proceed

parts.words: He's in suspense, as he's powerless to proceed
parts.note: a flier literally suspended beneath a frame and moving through the air with no engine

explanation.surface: A man is anxious and stuck because he can do nothing to move forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in suspense' and 'powerless' sound emotional; they mean hanging in a harness and having no motor.
explanation.definitionFit: This pilot hangs from an unpowered kite-like wing and flies on air currents alone.

clue.text: Around school-time children are found on the premises

indicators.note: the word for children goes round the word for a period of school

parts.note: minors are people under legal age, children
a term is a period of the school year

explanation.surface: During school periods, children turn up on the grounds of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'premises' suggests a building; in logic a syllogism's minor premise contains its minor term.
explanation.definitionFit: In a syllogism the minor term is the subject of the conclusion and appears in a premise.

clue.text: Come down in flames

explanation.surface: A description of something crashing to earth while burning.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to descend and land, as from a vehicle; also burning, on fire.

clue.text: Thoroughly cooked? Excellent

explanation.surface: A diner asks how a steak was prepared, then praises it.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat cooked right through is described this way, and the phrase is also a cry of praise.

clue.text: Former love no longer 15?

explanation.surface: A past sweetheart is asked whether the fire has gone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 points to the across answer meaning on fire; a flame that no longer burns is an old one.
explanation.definitionFit: An old flame is an ex-partner; read literally, it is a fire that has stopped burning.

clue.text: Kindly attitude is an asset in business

explanation.surface: A friendly manner pays off commercially.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodwill is friendly feeling; in accounting it is the value of a firm's reputation.

clue.text: Emphatically the sort of character to slope off

definitions.text: Emphatically the sort of character to slope off

parts.words: Emphatically the sort of character to slope off
parts.note: a printed letter style used for stress whose letters lean to the right

explanation.surface: A description of a person who is definitely the type to sneak away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like a person and 'slope off' like leaving; they mean a typeface letter and slanting.
explanation.definitionFit: This slanting typeface is used to give words emphasis in print.

clue.text: Prompt, as Hawking might be lecturing?

explanation.surface: A note that a famous physicist would arrive at his talk punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Hawking, the physicist, wrote A Brief History of Time, so a lecture of his would be about time.
explanation.definitionFit: Being punctual means arriving at the arranged moment; a talk about time is one on that subject.

clue.text: What typist needs to mind her p's and q's?

definitions.text: What typist needs to mind her p's and q's?

parts.words: What typist needs to mind her p's and q's?
parts.note: on a keyboard the outermost keys of the top row are struck with the smallest digit of each hand

explanation.surface: A question about what a secretary needs to behave politely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mind her p's and q's' is the idiom for good manners; here it means operating the P and Q keys.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest digit of each hand, the pinkie, strikes the keys at the ends of a keyboard row.

clue.text: Advantage no old boy's taken up

indicators.note: in a down answer the pieces are read upwards, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A school alumnus refuses to accept a benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns NOOB around to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A boon is a blessing or benefit, something that helps.

clue.text: Raise wage

explanation.surface: An instruction to increase pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wage' is the verb, as in waging war, not pay.
explanation.definitionFit: To levy is to raise a tax or troops; it also means to wage, as in levy war.

clue.text: Swear mildly, needing to make repair

explanation.surface: Someone curses gently because they have to fix something.
explanation.definitionFit: Darn is a mild oath replacing damn; it is also mending a hole by stitching.

clue.text: Read back to you it should seem the same

definitions.text: Read back to you it should seem the same

parts.words: Read back to you it should seem the same
parts.note: a word or phrase whose letters read in reverse order match its forward reading

explanation.surface: A note that when something is read aloud to you again it ought to sound unchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read back' suggests repeating dictation; it means reading the letters from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Words such as level or radar spell the same in both directions, which is what this term means.

clue.text: Flower came up

explanation.surface: A plant emerged from the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose is a garden bloom; rose is also the past tense of rise, meaning ascended.

clue.text: Drug habit in UK ruled territory

explanation.surface: A narcotics problem in a British-governed colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Dependency is addiction; it is also a territory governed by another country.
